findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481–482: When no local Integration exists, the Integration.DoesNotExist handler advances the pipeline without verifying authenticated-user ownership, allowing a supplied installation ID to proceed before its webhook creates the local record.

goldens.comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481–482: When no local Integration exists, the Integration.DoesNotExist handler advances the pipeline without verifying authenticated-user ownership, allowing a supplied installation ID to proceed before its webhook creates the local record.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught at line 481-482, the code simply calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without verifying the authenticated user. This is in contrast to the case when the Integration DOES exist (lines 485-498), where there's explicit verification that `pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') != integration.metadata['sender']['login']`. The finding correctly identifies that when no local Integration record exists yet (before the webhook creates it), the pipeline advances without the ownership check, potentially allowing an attacker to proceed with an installation_id before proper verification.
